title: Highlight
coreMove: Select one daily center before urgent, satisfying, or joyful options get crowded out by whatever shouts first.
sourcePressure: The source sidecar points to the daily-priority mechanism: choose a Highlight using urgency, satisfaction, and joy, then schedule it as the day's center of gravity.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The wrong generic version says choose a top task. The specific move is to decide which kind of value should anchor this day and give that Highlight a real place on the calendar.
sourceAnchorsNote: source contains no named anecdote for this chapter

hook: three sticky notes on a desk

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: prevents the timestamp+named-protagonist template from dominating the chapter

exampleSpecs.domain: an avalanche forecaster choosing which field report anchors a storm morning
exampleSpecs.audience: a safety analyst pulled between live radio calls, model updates, and field observations
exampleSpecs.stakes: ski patrol opens the wrong slope if the most meaningful observation gets delayed
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she marks the ridge-crack photo as today's urgent Highlight, blocks the 9:00 forecast window, and lets minor radio replies wait until the report is drafted
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a frost-specked ridge photo clipped beside a snowpack model printout

exampleSpecs.domain: a pastry commissary lead testing a filling before bakery rollout
exampleSpecs.audience: a production lead balancing urgent orders with a satisfying product fix
exampleSpecs.stakes: six stores keep selling a pastry with a runny center if the test is postponed again
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he chooses the filling test for satisfaction rather than the loud packing queue, writes it as the Highlight on the batch board, and schedules one uninterrupted oven cycle
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a tray of split pastries cooling beside a stainless batch board

exampleSpecs.domain: a documentary subtitler preparing one festival cut for a director review
exampleSpecs.audience: a language specialist whose work mixes urgent caption fixes with careful meaning
exampleSpecs.stakes: a mistranslated idiom changes the tone of a survivor interview
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: before, she clears every easy caption typo first; after, she chooses the survivor interview idiom as the day's satisfaction Highlight and gives it the first quiet hour
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a subtitle timeline paused on a speaker's half-smile

exampleSpecs.domain: a youth soccer tournament director rebuilding the rain-delay bracket
exampleSpecs.audience: an event operator choosing among urgent complaints, satisfying order, and joyful player experience
exampleSpecs.stakes: families drive across town for matches that no longer exist if the bracket stays wrong
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after one chaotic Saturday, he identifies the bracket rebuild as the next day's Highlight and schedules it before answering parent complaints
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a damp bracket sheet curling at the corner of a folding table

exampleSpecs.domain: a specialty print-house buyer resolving one missing paper-stock order
exampleSpecs.audience: a logistics worker tempted to treat all open requests equally
exampleSpecs.stakes: a museum catalog run stalls if the rare paper stock is buried under easy supply approvals
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he predicts the easy approvals will feel productive but not change the day, then selects the paper-stock order as the urgent Highlight and moves its mill call to the first block
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a torn paper swatch taped beside a stack of purchase approvals

exampleSpecs.domain: a botanical garden greenhouse manager planning a rare orchid transfer
exampleSpecs.audience: a caretaker deciding whether joy can legitimately anchor the day
exampleSpecs.stakes: a fragile orchid bloom is missed if routine watering rounds always take first claim
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she chooses the orchid transfer as a joy Highlight, writes the exact 2:30 window on the greenhouse slate, and moves routine watering around it
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a pale orchid spike tied to a bamboo splint under misted glass

skillTargets: choose a Highlight based on urgency, satisfaction, or joy in mixed-pressure scenarios
distinguish a Highlight from a task list item or vague goal
decide where a Highlight belongs on a real schedule
evaluate when a joyful Highlight is legitimate rather than indulgent drift

tryThisNowSpec: Scan today's remaining commitments and choose one Highlight by naming its reason: urgent, satisfying, or joyful. Put it into the smallest real calendar space you can still protect.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm -- a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following 'concrete anchor -> abstract rule -> elaboration'
